hash_lock.encoding: lowercase hex over complete raw-layer file bytes
hash_lock.batch_baseline_recipe: sha256 of the UTF-8 concatenation of `<role>\t<path>\t<source_sha256>\n` for every entry in order_index order (batch 02: three extraction rows, no probe rows)
hash_lock.batch_baseline_reproduce: { for f in content/brain/books/do-it-java/chap05.md content/brain/books/do-it-java/chap06.md content/brain/books/do-it-java/chap07.md; do printf "extraction\t%s\t%s\n" "$f" "$(shasum -a 256 "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; done; } | shasum -a 256
hash_lock.book_corpus_recipe: sha256 of the UTF-8 concatenation of `<path>\t<source_sha256>\n` for all 27 content/brain/books Markdown files in LC_ALL=C path order
hash_lock.batch_baseline_role: deterministic source baseline and sample-seed INPUT. It is NOT the AC-15 `sample.json` seed.
hash_lock.seed_use: CORRECTED (see independent verification F1). batch_baseline_sha256 pins the exact source bytes this inventory measured, so any source drift invalidates the inventory and any sample derived downstream of it. It is not itself the AC-15 seed. computeBatchSample() in tooling/brain/knowledge.mjs derives the U3 `sample.json` seed as sha256 of stable JSON over { batch_id, approved_knowledge_tree_sha256, batch_manifest_sha256, proposal_manifest_sha256 }. The source baseline reaches that seed only transitively, by being carried inside the future batch manifest, and the actual seed cannot exist until candidate authoring and proposal generation produce a proposal manifest. Batch 01 shows the distinction concretely: its inventory baseline is 5ef8fb7f741e627def5cda6fd5202c7a60193cfc36cd84c39cc0344f334ad99d while its realised U3 sample seed is a45086bd53ebdadd5cf3814c2377d32fcfdd0fcf11a541213d2ea299267a4e19. Let `knowledge.mjs sample` derive the seed; never hand-substitute this baseline for it.
hash_lock.drift_policy: fail-closed. Re-verify every source_sha256 immediately before propose and again before apply; a mismatch aborts the batch with zero writes.

line_count_definition: physical lines. A terminal newline terminates the last line and does not begin another, so line_count is NOT `split("\n").length`, which appends a phantom empty element for newline-terminated files. All three extraction sources end without a terminal newline, so their counts (908 / 572 / 674, total 2,154) are unchanged under this definition; the seven newline-terminated files in the corpus lock were corrected downward by one (independent verification F2). line_count is descriptive metadata and is not an input to batch_baseline_sha256 or book_corpus_sha256.

rejection_probe_policy.justification: CORRECTED (see independent verification F5). The Book corpus contains four frontmatter-only Markdown files with 0 body bytes each, of which exactly three are chapter files eligible as file-level probes: headfirst/chap01.md, kafka/chap03.md and kafka/chap04.md. All three are already hash-locked as book-batch-01 rejection probes inside an unresolved U3 packet. Adopting them here would couple batch 02 to a batch-01 outcome in both directions: if batch 01 is applied they are spent, and if batch 01 is rejected they are contested. The fourth frontmatter-only file, content/brain/books/index.md, is the root landing page; it is excluded as structural-landing-page and is not a valid extraction or probe candidate under the stated evidence rule, so it does not add a fourth probe option. Batch 02 therefore takes no file-level probe.

selection_rationale.scheduling_hint: Plan §Phase 5 initial scheduling hint ranks Book first, and the book-batch-01 inventory named chap05-07 as the recommended batch 02. This lane inventories that recommendation; it does not ratify batch 01.
selection_rationale.primary: chap05-07 (클래스와 객체 1·2, 배열과 ArrayList) are the OOP foundation arc that sits directly upstream of the applied pilot chapter chap08 (상속과 다형성). They supply the object/class/instance/constructor/static/array vocabulary that the applied java.oop.* concepts already presuppose but never define, so the batch fills a real hole under an already-populated namespace.
selection_rationale.path_coverage: Batch 02 is dominated by `create` under new namespaces (java.oop.*, java.memory.*, java.pattern.*, java.collection.*, java.keyword.*). Its distinctive test is the stub-promotion path: java.memory.garbage-collection is an applied concept whose proposal_kind is `stub`, and chap05/chap06 carry the first substantive heap/GC evidence in the Book corpus.
selection_rationale.bounded: Three extraction files, 57,373 bytes, 65 heading scopes of which 53 carry prose. This is roughly 1.75x the batch-01 surface and is the largest slice in the plan; see preconditions B2 for the review-load advisory and the optional 02a/02b split.
selection_rationale.probes: No file-level probes; 12 in-source zero-evidence scopes provide negative coverage instead. See rejection_probe_policy.
rejected_alternatives: Waiting for batch 01 to be applied before inventorying: inventory is read-only and hash-locked, so it is safe to produce now. Only candidate authoring is gated (precondition B1).

Splitting chap07 (배열과 ArrayList) into its own batch: chap07 opens java.collection.*, a namespace with no overlap against chap05/chap06. Defensible, but the dispatched scope for batch 02 is the three-file arc, so the split is recorded as an advisory rather than applied.

expected_flagged_for_full_review.sample_quota_recipe: CORRECTED (see independent verification F4). computeBatchSample() sets quota = min(unflagged_pool, max(5, ceil(0.10 * unflagged_pool))). The 10% applies to the UNFLAGGED pool, not to total proposals. Category coverage can then add one extra draw per proposal kind absent from the quota slice, so the discretionary count is a floor, not a ceiling. Batch 01 realised quota 5 from an unflagged pool of 7.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.estimated_u3_review_load: CORRECTED (see independent verification F4). ESTIMATE ONLY, not a mechanical derivation. Under the explicit and unproven assumption that each of the 16 low-evidence scopes yields exactly one flagged proposal, and a midpoint forecast of ~32 proposals, the unflagged pool would be ~32 - 16 = 16, quota = max(5, ceil(0.10 * 16)) = max(5, 2) = 5, and the reviewed set would be ~16 mandatory + 5 discretionary = ~21 proposals, plus any category-coverage top-ups. Two caveats bound this: (1) scope count does not map one-to-one to proposals - one proposal may cite several scopes, and conflict / provenance flags arise from causes unrelated to prose volume; batch 01 is the counterexample, where 6 low-evidence scopes produced 12 flagged proposals out of 19. (2) The comparison baseline is batch-01's REALISED U3 sample of 17 of 19 (12 mandatory + 5 discretionary), not the inventory-era estimate of ~10. So ~21 versus 17 is roughly 1.24x, NOT 'about double'. See precondition B2.

preconditions.statement: Book batch 01 is unresolved at U3. Its packet proposes 19 candidates (15 new ids across java.oop.*, java.keyword.*, java.pattern.*, software.practice.*, plus 4 updates), applied = false, run_state = none. None of those ids exist in content/brain/knowledge/ today.
preconditions.consequence: CORRECTED (see independent verification F3). If batch-02 candidate authoring runs first, the two batches author into java.oop.* and java.pattern.* against different views of the concept index, so whichever applies second is liable to concept_id / canonical_path collisions or to duplicating a mechanism batch 01 already named under a different id. The engine does NOT silently accept that: two packets authored against the same pre-batch tree cannot both apply once one of them changes the tree. The second apply is refused and the packet must be regenerated. The cost of ignoring B1 is therefore stale, throwaway authoring and a forced regeneration cycle, not an undetected corrupt merge.
engine_gates_that_do_catch_it: proposal generation builds a combined approved + proposal concept index and writes collision-report.json; a non-zero collision count fails verification
each batch proposal manifest binds approved_knowledge_tree_sha256 at generation time

apply runs per-target guards first (target_exists and target_before_sha256 per canonical path), then refuses with 'apply refused: approved knowledge content changed after proposal generation' if the whole-tree digest moved
apply re-checks link closure against the then-current approved index, so an approved document may not link to a concept the review left unapproved
preconditions.residual_risk_after_gates: Semantic duplication under two different ids that never collide on id or path would survive automated gates; that is a review-time judgement call, which is a further reason to sequence the batches rather than a claim that no gate exists.
preconditions.resolution: Proceed with batch-02 candidate authoring only after book-batch-01 U3 has been resolved and either (a) applied, in which case re-derive the approved concept index and re-check batch-02 ids against the 15 new ids, or (b) rejected, in which case batch 02 becomes the first claimant of java.oop.* / java.pattern.* and must be re-scoped accordingly. Either outcome changes batch-02 authoring; neither is assumed here.
preconditions.not_blocking: This inventory. Source inventory, hashing and scope indexing are read-only and outcome-independent, which is why this manifest exists now.

preconditions.severity_note: CORRECTED (see independent verification F4). Downgraded from `blocking` to `advisory`. B2 is an owner sizing decision to take before candidate authoring, not a mechanical correctness gate: nothing in the engine or in the measured numbers makes a single three-file batch 02 invalid. B1 remains the only sequencing blocker.
preconditions.statement: Sizing advisory. Batch 02 is the largest slice so far: 65 scopes versus batch-01's 37, 53 prose-bearing scopes versus 31, 57,373 bytes versus batch-01's smaller surface, and a forecast of 24-38 accepted candidates against batch-01's 14-22 (realised 19). It carries 16 low-evidence scopes under the 0 < prose_lines <= 3 rule versus batch-01's 6.
preconditions.consequence: CORRECTED. Under plan §5.1 one critical issue rejects the whole batch, so a larger packet has a larger regeneration blast radius. The magnitude was previously overstated. Corrected arithmetic: assuming one flagged proposal per low-evidence scope and a ~32-proposal midpoint, the unflagged pool is ~16 and the engine's quota is max(5, ceil(0.10 * 16)) = 5 - the 10% applies to the unflagged pool, not to total proposals - giving a reviewed set of roughly 16 + 5 = 21, plus any category-coverage top-ups. Batch-01's realised U3 sample was 17 of 19 (12 mandatory + 5 discretionary), so ~21 versus 17 is about 1.24x, not about double. The scope-to-proposal mapping is itself an assumption: batch 01 produced 12 flagged proposals from only 6 low-evidence scopes, so flags do not track low-evidence scopes one-to-one in either direction.
preconditions.required_before: candidate authoring (as a decision, not as a gate)
preconditions.resolution: Owner decision: author chap05-07 as one batch, or split into 02a (chap05, 29 scopes) and 02b (chap06+chap07, 36 scopes). The split remains a reasonable way to bound rejection/regeneration blast radius, and it stays available at any time because per-file hashes and scopes are recorded separately. The dispatched scope for this lane is the three-file arc, so this manifest inventories all three and takes no position on the split.
